title: DVT and PE: acute, chronic or history
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for pulmonary embolism.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F.

HPI: [Copied Forward] Patient is an 89-year-old female presenting with shortness of breath and chest pain. Imaging confirmed an acute pulmonary embolism two weeks ago. No signs of heart strain were noted on the initial CT. Patient was started on anticoagulation.

[Update] The patient reports she is feeling much better today. She denies any new shortness of breath or worsening chest pain. She is tolerating her current medication well and has not experienced any bleeding.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative
Respiratory: Negative
Cardiovascular: Negative
Gastrointestinal: Negative
Musculoskeletal: Negative
Neurological: Negative

Medication List:
- Apixaban 5mg twice daily

Exam:
General: Well-appearing, alert and oriented x3.
Respiratory: Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezes or rales.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. No murmurs.
Extremities: No edema noted.

Assessment:
1. Acute pulmonary embolism. Patient is in the first months of anticoagulant treatment and is currently stable.

Plan:
1. Continue Apixaban as prescribed.
2. Follow up in 4 weeks for routine monitoring.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, MD
May 14, 2026
explanations: Acute pulmonary embolism without acute cor pulmonale, under initial treatment: I26.99 (HCC 267).
